title: The Portrait of Saint Alder's
premise: Rafael Halloran, the meticulous archivist of Saint Alder's Cathedral, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after Dean Wexler's funeral—a letter claiming the dean's death was no accident and implicating the cathedral's most beloved figures. As Rafael digs into three years of deliberately misfiled records, they uncover a pattern of suppressed scandals, a locked crypt holding more than relics, and a town that closed its collective eyes decades ago. When the trial of an innocent man approaches, Rafael must choose between protecting the institution that gave them refuge and exposing the truth, culminating in the opening of the crypt before the court convenes—where the real killer's name is written in the dean's own hand.
about_author: Jonah Ashgrove is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent six years cataloguing documents no one was meant to read. They write mysteries about institutions, memory, and the quiet violence of good reputations.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Silence
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Establishes Rafael's ordered world at Saint Alder's: cataloguing, avoiding the townsfolk, keeping the crypt key untouched. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—Rafael has made invisibility an art form, and believes it protects them.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A confession letter arrives, postmarked the day after Dean Wexler's funeral, unsigned, claiming the death was murder. Rafael's hands shake as they file it—and then unfile it. The beat is dread breaking through routine.

chapters.title: Everyone Loved Him
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The funeral's aftermath: mourners perform grief while Canon Merrick watches Rafael too closely. Rafael notices the visitor log from the dean's final week has pages removed. Beat: first suspicion that the institution itself is lying.

chapters.title: The Misfiled Years
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Searching their own archive, Rafael finds deliberate misfilings—three years of documents shuffled by someone with archival knowledge. Only two people could have done it. Beat: paranoia; the sanctuary of order becomes evidence of conspiracy.

chapters.title: A Name in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Detective Ilsa Voss, investigating quietly. She interviews Rafael, who lies badly about the letter. Voss reveals a man, Tomas Reyes, will be tried for the dean's death in six weeks. Beat: Rafael realizes silence makes them complicit.

chapters.title: The Crypt Key
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael learns the crypt has been sealed since 1987—not for preservation, but by order of a bishop whose papers are also missing. They steal a wax impression of the key. Beat: crossing the line from observer to participant.

chapters.title: What the Choir Knew
chapters.summary: Choir mistress Edith Marlowe's POV. A retired singer remembers the last time the crypt opened: a boy chorister died, ruled accidental. Edith has kept quiet for forty years out of loyalty to the cathedral. Beat: loyalty as a slow poison.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael traces the confession letter's paper stock to the cathedral's own supply closet—the confessor works inside. Meanwhile someone searches Rafael's office at night. Beat: hunted hunter; fear sharpens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bishop's Box
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the diocesan annex, Rafael finds the missing bishop's papers: the 1987 boy's death involved the then-dean—Wexler himself, who helped bury it. Beat: the beloved dead man is revealed as both victim and accomplice.

chapters.title: Tomas Reyes
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss visits Reyes in custody; he claims he saw someone leaving the tower that night but stayed silent because the person saved his brother's life once. Beat: the cost of debts and silence mirrors Rafael's own.

chapters.title: Merrick's Kindness
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Canon Merrick offers Rafael a promotion and a transfer—generous, urgent, wrong. He knows what Rafael has found. Rafael accepts, buying time. Beat: corruption wears a warm face; guilt over the deception.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith admits she wrote the letter—she saw the killer too, forty years ago and again last month—but she cannot say the name aloud because he is her nephew. Beat: love versus truth made flesh.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A threatening note appears in Rafael's filing cabinet, alphabetized under H. Whoever it is knows the archive intimately. Rafael sets a trap with a false document. Beat: turning surveillance into strategy.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The false document is moved overnight; Voss stakes out the archive and catches the sexton, Bram Otley—but Bram was only retrieving something hidden there years ago: photographs. Beat: another layer peels away; the web widens.

chapters.title: Photographs, 1987
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The photos show the dead chorister alive hours after his 'death'—smuggled away, not murdered, by people protecting him from someone worse. The cover-up hid a rescue. Beat: moral vertigo; every secret had two faces.

chapters.title: Who Benefited
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Following money and motive, Rafael lands on the one figure untouched by suspicion: the cathedral's treasurer, Aldous Fenwick, whose family fortune was built on the orphanage where the boy fled. Beat: cold clarity; the pattern completes.

chapters.title: Night in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Confronted, Fenwick corners Rafael among the shelves—first charming, then menacing, revealing he's known about Rafael's digging for weeks. Rafael escapes through the bell tower. Beat: terror; the stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: The Trial Begins
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Reyes's trial opens; testimony collapses under Voss's doubts, but without evidence the case may end in conviction anyway. Voss risks her career by meeting Rafael off the record. Beat: alliance forged in desperation.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. With Voss and Edith, Rafael opens the crypt at dawn. Inside: the sealed 1987 record, the boy's true testimony naming Fenwick's father—and Wexler's recent follow-up notes, hidden where only the archivist would look. Beat: awe and horror; the dead testify.

chapters.title: Fenwick's Fall
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Armed with the crypt evidence, Voss arrests Fenwick mid-service before the entire congregation. He confesses with terrifying calm—he killed Wexler to keep the family's buried crime buried. Beat: cathartic exposure; power stripped bare.

chapters.title: Reyes Walks Free
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The charges against Reyes are dropped; he thanks Rafael without knowing why he needed thanking. Merrick resigns rather than face reform. Rafael declines the transfer. Beat: bittersweet justice; institutions bend slowly, if at all.

chapters.title: Recatalogued
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael refiles the archive honestly for the first time, creating a new index titled 'Truths, Unsealed,' and leaves the crypt door unlocked. Final beat: memory honored instead of managed; invisibility traded for integrity.
